newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-YOUNG TAKES SEVEN AS PAKISTAN OUT FOR 299.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG TAKES SEVEN AS PAKISTAN OUT FOR 299.

text.p: Tasmania all-rounder Shaun Young snared seven wickets as Pakistan were bowled out for 299 on the first day of their four-day match at Bellerive Oval on Thursday.
Young finished with seven for 64 from 18.3 overs, his best figures in first-class cricket, against a weakened Pakistan side without opener Aamir Sohail.
Sohail needed 10 stitches in a head wound after slipping in a dressing room mishap following his side's seven-wicket defeat by West Indies on Tuesday.

Tasmania dismissed Pakistan midway through the final session and in reply were 73 for one at stumps. Opener Jamie Cox was unbeaten on 39 and night-watchman Daniel Marsh was two after Dene Hills fell to Mushtaq Ahmed for 29.
Medium-pacer Young opened his account by trapping spin bowler Saqlain Mushtaq for 10. Saqlain was sent in to open the innings in place of Sohail after Pakistan captain Wasim Akram won the toss.
The Tasmanian then had new batsman Ijaz Ahmed caught in the slips by Ricky Ponting for a duck with his next ball.
Young missed his hat trick but went on to dismiss test batsmen Inzamam-ul-Haq for seven and Mohammad Wasim for 25 and wicketkeeper Moin Khan for 24.
Pakistan's total would have been much smaller but for a 74-run partnership between Shahid Afridi and Mushtaq for the seventh wicket.
Afridi, holder of the world record for the fastest limited overs century, hit a typically quickfire 80 while Mushtaq scored 65 before becoming Young's sixth victim.
